screens_reviewed: Single full-page capture of the audit Weighting step (step 2 of 9) on iPad in dark theme: stack header, step chip + progress card, 9 step pills, the 'Youth weighting' card with three 5-domain importance ChoiceQuestions visible, and the fixed Back / Save & exit / Next footer.
verdict: Functionally complete and on-brand: content is centered and width-constrained via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, the footer is safe-area aware, and the dark palette reads cleanly. But this is a scaled-up phone layout rather than an iPad-adapted one: typography uses hardcoded pixel sizes with no tablet base-scale, the static designSystem import bypasses the ScaledText/useDesignSystem accessibility path, and the single-column option lists plus a default ~1040px content track leave wide rows and large dead horizontal space that a 2-column option grid or a step rail would use better.

critical_issues.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx — module import and every Text/Paragraph
critical_issues.issue: The screen imports the static light-only `designSystem` constant instead of the `useDesignSystem()` hook, so it never reacts to the user's fontScale or dyslexic-font preferences, and all type is set with fixed pixel literals (e.g. StepHeader title fontSize={30}, Card title fontSize={22}, QuestionCard label fontSize={16}). On iPad these stay at phone sizes — the TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3 multiplier defined for tablets is never applied because the shared ScaledText primitive is not used here.
critical_issues.evidence: audit-placeId-step.md:23 (`import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system"`), :549 fontSize={28}, :614 fontSize={30}, :1094 fontSize={22}, :1169 fontSize={16}; core.md:792 TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE=1.3; core.md ScaledText/AppButton are the shared scaled primitives this screen does not use
critical_issues.fix: Switch to `const designSystem = useDesignSystem()` and render text via the shared ScaledText/ScaledParagraph primitives (or multiply font sizes by designSystem.fontScale and the tablet base scale), so iPad text scales up and respects accessibility preferences instead of rendering at phone sizes.

critical_issues.issue: OptionGrid always renders options in one vertical YStack and the WeightingStep stacks every domain question in a single column regardless of layout.isTablet. On iPad this produces very wide, sparse option rows (three short choices like 'Very important to me' each spanning the full ~1040px content track) and a tall single-column scroll where a 2-column option grid or a 2-up question layout would use the canvas. No isTablet branch exists in this file.
critical_issues.evidence: image (full-width option buttons with large empty right space); audit-placeId-step.md:1244-1271 OptionGrid (single YStack, no isTablet branch); :812-878 WeightingStep maps domains into one column
critical_issues.fix: When layout.isTablet, lay short-choice options out in a 2-column wrap (XStack flexWrap with flexBasis ~48%) and/or render the weighting domains in a two-column grid, so the iPad shows an adapted form rather than a stretched phone column.

improvements.suggestion: The container is built with no `maxWidth`, so it defaults to contentMaxWidth (1040 on narrow tablet, up to 1200 wide) rather than the form-oriented formMaxWidth (600). A single-column survey form reads better and keeps option rows a comfortable measure if it passes `maxWidth: layout.formMaxWidth` for this form-style screen.
improvements.evidence: audit-placeId-step.md:434-437 (options omit maxWidth); core.md:972-973 contentMaxWidth vs formMaxWidth tokens

improvements.suggestion: The 9 wrap-around step pills behave like a compact phone wizard. On the iPad canvas a persistent left step rail (master-detail) or a single full-width segmented progress bar would give clearer wayfinding and exploit the horizontal space instead of a wrapped pill cloud above the form.
improvements.evidence: image (two rows of small step pills); audit-placeId-step.md:669-703 flexWrap pill row with no isTablet treatment

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used is (none): this screen hand-rolls Card, Button, Badge/pill, Field and Text styling inline with the static `designSystem` tokens instead of the shared components/ui primitives (Card.tsx, Button.tsx/AppButton, Badge.tsx, Field.tsx, ScaledText.tsx) that exist in core.md — a consistency and accessibility gap (AppButton documents the 52pt target and ScaledText carries fontScale).

Spacing and radii come from the design-system constants (radii.xl/lg, px/py size tokens) rather than raw pixels, so token discipline for spacing is good; the gap is typography (fixed fontSize literals) and the missing hook.
FooterNav correctly uses layout.screenPaddingHorizontal and insets.bottom + 12 for the bottom safe area (audit-placeId-step.md:1678-1681), so the absolute footer is safe-area aware.
platform_notes: iPad adaptation is partial: content centering/width-constraint via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle is present (audit-placeId-step.md:434), but there is no media/breakpoint branching inside the route for columns, and typography does not pick up the tablet base scale, so the page reads as a scaled-up phone screen.
This is a full-screen pushed route (audit/[placeId] registered with headerShown:false at root then a per-screen header), not a modal/sheet, so iPad modal-sizing concerns do not apply here.

Safe-area: insets.bottom is consumed in the footer; the top relies on the native stack header plus the root Stack contentStyle paddingTop:20 (core.md:1378), which is adequate for iPad which has no notch.
not_assessable: Exact rendered font sizes and whether the tablet base scale is applied elsewhere cannot be confirmed from a single capture; claim is grounded in the code path (static designSystem import, fixed fontSize literals).
Precise WCAG contrast ratios for the dark palette pairs (e.g. mutedForeground #A7A99F on surface #1E201C) are estimates; nothing in the capture is clearly below AA, so no contrast issue is flagged.
Landscape / split-view / Stage Manager behavior and the appearance of later domain steps (3-8) are not shown.
Runtime states (saving spinner, sync error NoticeCard, alert on incomplete step) are not visible in this capture.
score_rationale: Usable with clear, real problems. The form works, is on-brand, centered, and safe-area aware, but it is a scaled-up phone layout for iPad: fixed pixel typography with no tablet scaling, the static designSystem import bypassing the ScaledText/useDesignSystem accessibility path, and single-column option lists on a wide default content track that a 2-column grid or step rail should fill. Solid foundation, but multiple iPad-specific adaptation gaps keep it in the 5-6 band rather than 7-8.
